subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `direct.<peer>.tools` and `toolsBySender` be an enforced per-DM security boundary, with the same trust and precedence guarantees as group tool policy?
rationale: The schema and types already expose the config, but making it effective changes security-control enforcement for existing installs; automation should not choose between enforcing, retiring, or redesigning that boundary without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Enforce Direct Tool Policy
options.body: Implement a direct/DM-aware resolver for Telegram that honors exact direct entries before wildcard defaults while preserving sender and account scoping.

options.title: Retire Or Clarify The Field
options.body: If per-DM tool policy is not intended, remove or doctor-migrate the misleading schema/type surface and document the supported alternatives.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Binding Policy
options.body: Defer this to a broader binding/session policy design only if maintainers want one cross-channel authorization model rather than a Telegram-specific fix.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Implement a direct/DM-aware resolver for Telegram that honors exact direct entries before wildcard defaults while preserving sender and account scoping.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to shared policy/security layering, where recent history shows scoped group policy and trusted group fact work.
